title: Raw Integer Time Durations
pattern: Passing time durations as raw integer primitives representing seconds, milliseconds, or clock cycles.
why_bad: The scale of the value is opaque to the compiler. Developers must rely on name conventions (e.g., `ms` suffix), which easily rot, causing timing misalignment if a caller passes seconds instead of milliseconds.
detection: Function signatures taking integer primitives (`u64`, `u32`) where parameter names indicate a time duration scale (`ms`, `secs`, `duration`).
counterexample: Low-level micro-controller code or drivers executing hardware-level busy loops using raw instruction cycles.
source: *Understanding Software Dynamics* by Richard L. Sites (p. 129).
